items.title: Determinant-line holonomy for a global anomaly test
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current batch-41 local-anomaly Definition inspected and used only to distinguish its infinitesimal class from determinant-line holonomy. Its Step 1 readiness record is missing; effective dependency level recomputed as 4 from the current supplier graph.
items.statement:
Fix an even integer $d\ge2$, a compact smooth oriented Riemannian $d$-manifold $M$ without boundary with a specified spin structure, a smooth principal right $G$-bundle $P\to M$ with connection $A$, and a unitary finite-dimensional complex representation $R:G\to U(V_R)$. Let $E_R=P\times_R V_R$ be the associated Hermitian bundle. Let $S^+$ and $S^-$ be the associated bundles of the two half-spin representations of $\operatorname{Spin}(d)$. The chiral Dirac operator is the first-order operator

$$D^+_{A,R}:H^1(M;S^+\otimes E_R)\longrightarrow L^2(M;S^-\otimes E_R),$$

where $H^1$ and $L^2$ are the first Sobolev and square-integrable completions for the fixed Riemannian metric. Assume the operator is Fredholm. Its inverse determinant line is

$$\mathcal L_A=\left(\det_{\mathbb C}\ker D^+_{A,R}\right)^*\otimes\det_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D^+_{A,R},$$

with $\det_{\mathbb C}W=\bigwedge^{\dim_{\mathbb C}W}_{\mathbb C}W$. For a smooth family of such Fredholm operators over a parameter manifold, use the Quillen metric and the Bismut–Freed unitary connection on this line bundle. For a real or pseudoreal fermionic quadratic form, the Pfaffian line replaces the determinant line and carries its induced Hermitian metric and unitary connection.

Let $\mathcal A(P)$ be the affine space of smooth connections on $P$, and let $\mathcal G(P)$ be the group of smooth bundle automorphisms covering the identity on $M$. A gauge arrow $u:A\to A^u$ induces a unitary map $u_*:\mathcal L_A\to\mathcal L_{A^u}$ by its action on kernel and cokernel. A closed loop in background/gauge-field space consists of a smooth path $A_t$ in $\mathcal A(P)$, $0\le t\le1$, and an endpoint gauge arrow $u:A_0\to A_1$. Let $\mathrm{PT}_{A_t}:\mathcal L_{A_0}\to\mathcal L_{A_1}$ be parallel transport and $u_*:\mathcal L_{A_0}\to\mathcal L_{A_1}$ the endpoint gauge map. The closed-loop automorphism is $u_*^{-1}\circ\mathrm{PT}_{A_t}$ on $\mathcal L_{A_0}$. Its scalar is the holonomy $\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L)\in U(1)$. Fix the regularization and local-counterterm convention before comparing this loop phase with the infinitesimal local anomaly; the holonomy itself is additional global loop data.

items.title: Relative boundary theory and invertible anomaly inflow
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional line-duality and cancellation Definition, with the batch-41 local-anomaly interface inspected and explicitly not used to classify global holonomy. Its Step 1 readiness record is missing; effective dependency level recomputed as 5.
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$. Let $Y$ be a compact oriented smooth spin $(d+1)$-manifold with boundary $M=\partial Y$, using the outward-normal-first boundary orientation. A background $b$ consists of the metric, spin structure, and any specified principal-bundle connections and associated fields on $Y$; its restriction to $M$ is the boundary background. A $d$-dimensional boundary theory is **relative to an invertible bulk theory** when its partition value is a vector $Z_\partial(M,b|_M)$ in a specified one-dimensional Hermitian line $\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)$, and the bulk assigns the dual line $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}(M,b|_M)\cong\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)^*$ together with a vector $Z_{\mathrm{bulk}}(Y,b)$ in that line. The canonical evaluation

$$\mathrm{ev}:\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}(M,b|_M)\longrightarrow\mathbb C$$

then defines the combined scalar amplitude. Invertibility means that the bulk assigns a one-dimensional line to each closed $d$-dimensional boundary background and an isomorphism to each bordism map; orientation reversal replaces the assigned line by its dual. For a loop $\gamma$ of compatible background fields and endpoint gauge identifications, the boundary/bulk pair cancels that anomaly along $\gamma$ exactly when

$$\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L_\partial)\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}})=1.$$

The diagram records this condition: the vertical maps are the line evaluation at the two endpoints, and the top map is parallel transport on both lines.

~~~tikzcd
\mathcal L_{\partial,0}\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk},0}
  \arrow[r,"\mathrm{PT}^{\partial}_{\gamma}\otimes\mathrm{PT}^{\mathrm{bulk}}_{\gamma}"]
  \arrow[d,"\mathrm{ev}_0"'] &
\mathcal L_{\partial,1}\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk},1}
  \arrow[d,"\mathrm{ev}_1"] \\
\mathbb C \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}"'] & \mathbb C
~~~

items.title: A global SU(2) determinant-line phase and its mod-two inflow cancellation
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; the index-one equality remains an explicit source-supported hypothesis, and the batch-41 local-anomaly interface is used only to separate local scope from holonomy. Its Step 1 readiness record is missing; effective dependency level recomputed as 6.
items.statement: Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $M=S^4$ with its boundary orientation, a specified smooth Riemannian metric and standard spin structure, and let $E\to M$ be a smooth rank-two Hermitian bundle with structure group $SU(2)$ and smooth unitary connection $A$. Treat $SU(2)$ as a nondynamical background global symmetry and consider one massless left-handed Weyl fermion in the fundamental representation. Use the inverse determinant/Pfaffian line and the index-density normalization $I_6=[\widehat A(TM)\operatorname{ch}(E)]_6$ for its universal local anomaly polynomial, with $F_A$ anti-Hermitian and $\operatorname{ch}(E)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf 2}\exp(-F_A/(2\pi i))$. Assume the selected background is in the index-one sector, meaning the coupled chiral Dirac operator $D_A^+$ is Fredholm and $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}D_A^+=1$. For a proved concrete instance, assume full AC and take the unit round metric, $E=S^+$ and the positive-spin Levi-Civita connection: its complex chiral kernel has dimension $1$, its cokernel dimension $0$, and $\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-1$ in the convention $c(E)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$. The conditional conclusion below still applies to every stipulated index-one background; this concrete instance supplies that index by proof rather than as a physical postulate. Let $z=-I\in SU(2)$ act on the fermion fibers and form the corresponding order-two loop $\gamma_z$ of the background/gauge-field groupoid. Since $z$ acts as $-1$ in the fundamental representation, its action on this fermion is the same twist as $(-1)^F$; use the fermion-parity mapping-torus convention represented by $Y_z=S^4\times S^1$ with pulled-back gauge connection and periodic spinors around $S^1$. Equivalently, a central $z$ gauge clutch combined with an antiperiodic spin clutch has this periodic total fermion boundary condition. A periodic spin clutch combined with the same $z$ gauge clutch would instead give antiperiodic total fermions; the two conventions must not be conflated in an eta-holonomy formula. For $N\ge1$ independent identical Weyl doublets, the local polynomial vanishes and the boundary holonomy on this loop is $(-1)^N$. Adopt, for this test, a five-dimensional invertible bulk response with phase $Z_{\mathrm{bulk}}(Y_z,A)=(-1)^{N\operatorname{ind}_2D_{Y_z}}$, where $\operatorname{ind}_2D_{Y_z}=\dim_{\mathbb R}\ker D_{Y_z}\bmod2$ for the real Dirac realization; then the bulk phase is $(-1)^N$ and the combined boundary/bulk holonomy is $+1$. For the finite normalization check take $K$ to be a single-vertex ordered simplicial complex and the ordinary field groupoid $\mathcal F(K)=BC_2$, with one object and automorphism group $C_2=\{1,z\}$. The boundary line alone has no invariant scalar gauging weight when $N$ is odd, while the boundary line tensored with the inverse bulk line has the normalized finite groupoid sum $1/2$. Even $N$ cancels this tested anomaly; this statement does not exclude other global or local anomalies outside the stated model and loop.

items.title: One-instanton SU(2) sign cancelled by a mod-two-index bulk
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; worked application of the conditional global-anomaly test and finite BC2 normalization. It inherits the missing batch-41 Step 1 readiness input; effective dependency level recomputed as 7.
items.statement: Assume full AC and take the explicit unit round spin $S^4$ background with $E=S^+$ and its positive-spin Levi-Civita connection, one massless left-handed Weyl doublet of a nondynamical $SU(2)$ global symmetry, and the order-two central transformation $z=-I$ specified in the global-anomaly test. The local Hodge calculation gives complex chiral index $1$ and Chern number $-1$; pair the boundary determinant/Pfaffian line with the five-dimensional bulk whose test-loop phase is $(-1)^{\operatorname{ind}_2D_5}$. The boundary line has character $\chi(1)=1$, $\chi(z)=-1$; the mapping-torus mod-two index is $1$, so the bulk character is $\chi^{-1}=\chi$ and the combined character is trivial. The local index-density anomaly polynomial is zero. For the finite normalization check take a single-vertex complex $K$ and the ordinary field groupoid $\mathcal F(K)=BC_2$, with one object and automorphism group $C_2$. The combined unit weight is arrow-invariant and its normalized groupoid sum is $1/2$. Without the bulk, the odd boundary character is not a scalar invariant weight and no such finite gauging sum is defined. For two identical copies the boundary character itself is trivial and the same normalized groupoid sum applies. This example tests only the stated loop and does not establish that even copies have no other anomalies.
